title: Staged warm windows & buffer triggers by region (24mo)
summary: Working sheet to define warm standby windows, buffer triggers, and month-by-month regional GPU onboarding plan for NA / EU / APAC over the next 24 months. Focus on operational triggers (utilization/time), traffic profile splits, and prioritized model lanes for soft-launches.
body:
Purpose:
- Capture a pragmatic, trigger-driven plan for regional GPU capacity activation and warm standby windows across North America, Europe, and APAC for a ~24 month horizon.
- Make operational triggers explicit so SRE/infra schedulers can automate warm-ups, instance reservations, and cross-region fallbacks.
- Surface risks and quick mitigation playbooks we can test during next on-call drills.

Key assumptions (callouts):
- Baseline demand growth: +18% q/q for production traffic; heavy tail driven by 2 new enterprise customers in H2 2026.
- Average token-per-request growth: +8% over 12 months as customers roll out more complex prompts.
- Preferred HW mix: A100 (40%), H100 (35%), L4x (25%) across new orders; vendor lead times remain 8–14 weeks.
- We keep a minimum 10% pooled spare of active dedicated fleet on a rolling 7-day window (soft SLA for burst).

Executive summary (one-liner):
- Use two-tier warm strategy: short warm-window (24–72h) for predictable weekly surges; long warm-window (7–21d) for onboarding new customers or anticipated major feature launches.
- Triggers are primarily utilization-duration based (sustained utilization threshold) with secondary triggers for queue latency and customer commit signals (sales/CS).

Operational triggers (proposed):
- Short warm-window trigger: region average GPU utilization > 65% sustained for 36 hours OR p95 request latency > 180ms for 12 hours. Action: spin up reserved warm instances (target +12% capacity) and enable aggressive KV-prefix caching.
- Long warm-window trigger: region average GPU utilization > 75% sustained for 72 hours OR flagged enterprise on-boarding event (sales tag). Action: place vendor reservations / increase spot-to-reserved mix to secure capacity +30% for 14 days.
- Immediate throttle/fallback trigger: per-zone request queue depth > 1200 requests for 1 hour. Action: enable cross-region routing to warm standby (prefer same hemisphere), degrade heavy-compute model variants to quantized variant and notify SRE rotation.

Regional rollouts (month buckets are planning months from Mar-2026):
- North America (NA):
  - Mar–May 2026: focus on short warm-windows. Incremental onboarding: +120 A100 equiv. capacity (primarily burst pool).
  - Jun–Aug 2026: reserve runway for two enterprise launches (estimated +240 A100 equiv.). Prepare long warm-window reservations in early Jun.
  - Sep–Dec 2026: flatten growth; convert 40% of short warm pool into dedicated reserved slots based on utilization signals.
  - 2027 H1: tactical H100 procurement window (target +300 H100 equiv.) timed to expected increased multimodal traffic.

- Europe (EU):
  - Mar–Jun 2026: conservative growth; add +80 A100 equiv. with staggered 3-week warm windows to smooth lead time risk.
  - Jul–Oct 2026: enable long warm-window for EU-west to support enterprise compliance testing (on-demand encryption).
  - Nov 2026–Feb 2027: buffer consolidation—reserve a persistent +15% buffer on EU fleet for holiday traffic variance.

- APAC:
  - Mar–Jul 2026: prioritize spot and short warm-windows; vendor lead times longer so prefer flexible capacity (L4x for latency-sensitive web endpoints).
  - Aug–Dec 2026: staged reserved reservations for SEA and JP regions aligned with partner launches (+160 A100 equiv. across zones).
  - 2027: expand long warm-window policy in APAC to cover multi-week regional promotions.

Traffic profile per region (high level):
- NA: 55% latency-sensitive chat, 30% batch embeddings, 15% offline evals.
- EU: 45% latency-sensitive, 40% embeddings/rerank, 15% longer-context research workloads.
- APAC: 65% latency-sensitive web completions, 25% embeddings, 10% batch training proxies.

Capacity table (planned active capacity addition by period — A100 equivalent):
- Mar–May 2026: NA +120, EU +80, APAC +90
- Jun–Aug 2026: NA +240, EU +60, APAC +40
- Sep–Dec 2026: NA +150, EU +120, APAC +160
- Jan–Mar 2027: NA +100, EU +80, APAC +140
(Notes: "A100 equivalent" normalizes across H100/L4x based on token throughput estimates; procurement orders should include explicit equivalence ratios.)

Buffer sizing and justification:
- Weekly surge buffer: 12% of active fleet per region (short warm-window pool). Rationale: typical weekly peak multipliers observed = 1.08–1.12.
- Enterprise on-boarding buffer: 25–35% reserved capacity held for signed enterprise customers during their onboarding window.
- Strategic long runway: incremental 30% for major product launches (7–21d warm-window).

Risk register (top items):
- Vendor lead time spike: If lead times > 16 weeks, move to multi-vendor split and increase spot mix; escalate to procurement and finance.
- Overprovisioning cost drag: Monitor token-cost delta monthly; if cost per served token increases > 9% vs baseline, pause reserved conversions and re-evaluate quantization tradeoffs.
- Cross-region networking caps: We have limited egress headroom for APAC->NA fallback; ensure partner network allocation request (NetOps ticket) is created before enabling cross-region fallback.

Automation & playbooks (runbook snippets):
- Short warm-window playbook (SRE rotation): check utilization alert -> run infra script to spin warm pool -> run smoke test on sample prompts -> mark warm pool healthy -> notify #infra-warm-ops channel.
- Long warm-window playbook (procurement + infra): trigger procurement reservation workflow (PO, vendor confirmation) -> pre-stage images and model caches -> enable extended warm instances -> run canary traffic for 48h.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Finalize A100:H100:L4 equivalence ratios for billing and forecasting (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Add explicit network egress capacity targets for APAC fallback (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Simulate 72h sustained 75% util + sudden 30% traffic spike in chaos env (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Link the pricing/commitment impact matrix to finance model (JIRA-OPS-1248).

Appendix: key references and links
- Confluence: Infra Runway 2026 (CONFLUENCE-Infra-Runway-2026)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-1248 (procurement/reservations backlog)
- Slack threads: #infra-capacity, #sales-enterprise-onboarding (search for thread id: 2267)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally concise; it's a working-sheet for the next 8 planning syncs.
- Expect it to change after procurement confirms vendor leadtime updates in May.

Quick action items for next week:
- Marco: run updated throughput equivalency tests and post numbers by 2026-02-22.
- Priya: open NetOps egress capacity ticket for APAC fallback by 2026-02-20.
- Liam: schedule chaos test and add result template to linked artifacts.

-- end of sheet --
